why: Housing-finance borrower terminology as investor decks and annual reports print it (an HFC's customer mix: salaried vs self-employed borrowers; the deck's 'Product and customer mix' slide). It names the HFC's borrowers, not the base product's account, and the model must match it in the document.
The RBI Master Direction disclosure heading 'Customer complaints', quoted as the annual report prints it: the model must find that heading in the notes.

A path is accepted under the display folder (Companies/, what the tools answer with) or the folder the base store keeps (Customers/, what storage and older rows carry). Both name the same folder; the store's folder is base code, not the pack's to rename.
A hidden command-line alias (--customer-id / --customer), kept so an older call still works. It is suppressed from --help; --company-id is the only documented flag.

The row key's older name, in the one place readers learn it: rows written before migrations/0001_primary_context_entity.py still read as primary_context_entity, and a row carrying both keys with different values is refused. Writers never emit it. Drop this entry (and the constant) once the migration has been applied to every live data room.
